hints: Look closely at statement 1 and picture the active site holding two substrates in exactly the right position and orientation for a collision to work.
Remember what lowering activation energy does to the proportion of molecules able to react, and why our body temperature is enough when an enzyme is present.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - bringing molecules together**

Think of the enzyme as a helpful hand. It binds substrates in its active site so their reactive groups are held close together in the correct orientation.

This increases the chance of successful collisions, so statement 1 is true.

**Check statement 2 - more molecules can react**

Enzymes do not give molecules extra energy. They lower the activation energy, $E_a$, needed to start the reaction.

With a lower $E_a$, a much larger proportion of molecules already have sufficient energy to react at that moment, so statement 2 is true.

**Check statement 3 - reaction at lower temperature**

Without an enzyme, many reactions would need very high heating to give enough molecules the high $E_a$.

Because the enzyme lowers $E_a$, the reaction can proceed rapidly at a much lower temperature, such as body temperature, so statement 3 is true.

options.A: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true, so this combination is correct.
options.B: This misses out statement 3, which is true because lowering $E_a$ allows the reaction to work at body temperature.
options.C: This misses out statement 2, which is true because lower $E_a$ means more molecules have enough energy to react.
options.D: This misses out statement 1, which is true because the active site holds substrates close together in the correct orientation.
